front: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air?
Which processes release carbon dioxide into the air?
back: Respiration (plants, animals, decomposers), decomposition and combustion.

front: How does carbon pass along a food chain?
back: As organic compounds (carbohydrates, fats, proteins) when consumers eat other organisms.

front: Role of decomposers in the carbon cycle?
back: They feed on dead organisms and waste and release carbon dioxide by respiration.
From remains of organisms that were not decomposed (e.g. no oxygen), changed by heat and pressure over millions of years.
Burning a fuel in oxygen, releasing carbon dioxide and energy.

front: Approximate carbon dioxide concentration of the air?
Why is carbon dioxide higher among crops at night?
back: Respiration continues but there is no photosynthesis to remove carbon dioxide.
notes: It is lowest in the early afternoon.

front: Human activities that raise atmospheric carbon dioxide?
back: Burning fossil fuels (coal at Hwange, vehicle fuels), deforestation (for farmland, firewood, tobacco curing) and veld fires.

front: Two reasons deforestation increases carbon dioxide?
back: Fewer trees carry out photosynthesis; burning or rotting the wood releases its carbon.
